message:
fix(client): stop asking for a preview that is never going to come

Product 8, test 1, tool 1, build 1. This half is live: both clients call the new predicate.

Both of them throttled preview requests on the preview CACHE. A window whose preview never
arrives is not in that cache, so it fell straight past the throttle and was queued again on
every panel refresh -- forever. viewer_picker.cpp only skipped ids already in `thumbs`, and
the shared core only skipped ids where `thumbs_.count(id) != 0`, and both maps are written
exclusively inside `if (reply.present)`.

That is the client half of the window that stops answering WM_PRINT. The host is about to
start skipping such a window; without this the viewer would keep asking anyway, once per
refresh, each one a roundtrip on the control thread to be told no again.

The cache can say how fresh a preview is. It cannot say when we last asked, and those two come
apart exactly when asking does not work. So the attempt is now recorded separately -- for every
completed exchange, not just the ones that produced pixels -- and a failed attempt is throttled
on the host's cooldown rather than the five second refresh.

One predicate in a shared header rather than the same edit twice. Two clients had the same bug
for the same reason, and writing the rule down once is what stops it being fixed on one side
only. The order inside it is deliberate: a window that worked and then stopped has both a stale
preview and a recent failure, and checking the cache first would refresh it right back into the
cooldown.

The card now says which kind of empty it is. "미리보기 준비 중…" on a window the host has given
up on was the UI telling you to keep waiting for something that is not coming; a refused one
reads "미리보기 없음" and stays selectable, because no preview is not a reason to stop you
capturing the window.

Evidence: 13 new checks, and they fail for the right reason -- restoring the old cache-only
rule breaks 5 of them. Shared-core suite, picker gesture, selection gate, layout, empty state,
open chain and the isolated window-proc suite (42) all still pass. The label was rendered
through draw_overlay, the same function the product paints with, into
.claude/ui-preview/picker-thumb-refused.png: three states in one picture -- two real previews,
one refused, one still coming.

What that picture is not: the shipped viewer against a live host. It is the product's drawing
code rendered offscreen by a tool, which settles the wording and the layout and settles nothing
about a real session.
